Which extensions

Info

The menus list what belongs in the chosen Style; hover over an entry for what it is and which styles it fits. Tick Unlock to see everything: what fits the style is listed first and the rest follows under its own headings.

Unmarked extensions are heard in the Standard, Drop 2 and Drop 3 voicings. Shells, guide tones, the three-string guitar shapes and open chords are fixed sets of notes and stay as they are; Rootless voicings always carry a 9th and 13th. Chords written with an alteration (C7♭9, C7alt) are left alone.

Tick more rhythms or voicings and the band uses all of them. Ticked rhythms: the short swing figures are mixed bar by bar; the others (four to the bar, the Latin patterns, arpeggios) are kept for four bars at a time. With Rhythm on Varied, ticking rhythms limits it to just those.

Drums

The cymbal and the kit faders are in the Mixer.

Blend in more grooves

Congas

Mixer
Organ: tonebars, swell and Leslie
Info

Nine tonebars, each from 0 (pushed in, silent) to 8 (pulled out, full): 16′ an octave below, 5⅓′ a fifth above, 8′ the note itself, then 4′, 2⅔′, 2′, 1⅗′, 1⅓′ and 1′ above it. The first two are brown, the octaves white and the others black, as on the instrument. The chorus (C3), the tube drive and the speaker's own settings are under Tone (EQ) below, in the organ's amp. The organ does not respond to touch: its louds and softs are the swell pedal.

Tone (EQ)

Amp
Info

The clean and distorted electric guitars are the jazz guitar's samples played through an amp. When one of them is chosen above, its amp is listed under the EQ, stage by stage in the order the sound passes through: Input gain is how hard the amp is hit, Drive how much it distorts, Output level makes up the loudness afterwards. The EQ comes after the amp.

Five bands for each sound, remembered on this computer. Every band can be a bell (boost or cut around a frequency), a shelf (everything below or above it), or a cut (low cut removes what is below the frequency, high cut what is above; the amount does not apply). Width is how narrow the band is: low is broad, high is narrow. The settings belong to the sound, so the jazz guitar keeps its tone whatever tune or style is loaded.

Drum kit mix
Info

Each fader is on top of the Drums volume. The ride and crash start low because the sampled cymbals ring loudly; Reset faders returns to those settings.

Practice
Tempo change
then bpm
Info

The loop controls are in the Play panel at the top. Click a bar on the chart to start there, then press L and click the bar the loop should end on; L again turns the loop off and on. An end bar before the start loops over the end of the form (10 to 2 plays 10, 11, 12, 1, 2). With the loop on, a click moves its end and Shift-click moves its start. The second tempo box alternates with the first: 8 then -3 goes up 8, back 3, up 8, back 3. Stopping returns to the tempo you set.

Recording

Open the song file from Timestamp Notes (or a bar map) and the recording that goes with it. Clicking a bar on the chart then moves the recording there, and the band can follow the recording’s own tempo, bar by bar.

Save and load

Info

A setup is the changes (in their key and meter) with the tempo, style and every band, mixer and loop setting. Setups are kept in this browser on this device, and they also appear at the bottom of the Changes menu. Download all saves them as a file you can import on another device. To make one a built-in for everybody, press Show JSON for the defaults and send that text to whoever maintains the site: it is pasted into apps/shared/band/presets.js.

Notation
Show
Info

While the band plays, this shows the chorus you are about to hear: it is drawn before the chorus starts (during the count-in for the first one, and during the last bar of each chorus for the next) and stays while that chorus plays. Change a band setting and the bars not yet played are written again. With "Each repeat" tempo steps on, it shows the last chorus played instead. The piano is on a grand staff, with the bass clef holding what the left hand plays. Swung eighths are written as plain eighths; in 6/8 and 12/8 each beat is three written eighths. The bass is written an octave above where it sounds, and note lengths are rounded to eighths.

Melody

Write the melody there note by note, with these chords and sections.

Info

Press Record melody and play one note at a time along with the band. It plays the changes from the start bar with the count-in, and writes the first chorus. Bars that repeat in the changes (repeat signs, a section that comes round again) take the first time through. Only the bars you played are replaced, so you can record a section at a time by setting the start bar. A swung line is written as plain eighth notes; the band swings them when it plays the melody back. The melody follows the bar numbers: it is dropped if the number of bars changes, and moves with the Key menu. The ABC you edit above does not change; Copy the ABC with the melody, or Download it, to keep the notes.

Export MIDI

Exports the notes the band actually played, with the swing written into the timing. If nothing has been played yet, the bars are generated fresh with the current settings.

Edit the changes (ABC)
Paste ChordPro

Each line of words is a bar per chord, as on the Notation page; a line of bars ([G] | [C] [D] |) is played as written. {start_of_verse}, {start_of_chorus} or {c: Bridge} start sections; {time:}, {key:}, {tempo:} and {title:} are read. Chords over words copied from Ultimate Guitar work too. The result replaces the ABC below.

Info

The chord symbols in quotes are what the band reads. Where a symbol sits in the bar sets the beat it lands on, so "Cm7"z2 "F7"z2 gives each chord two beats. The rests only fill out the bar. A line such as P:Verse or P:Chorus names the section that starts at the next bar: the drummer fills into each one, a section called Chorus is played up, and the Sections menu by the Play button can hold each section until you press Next. "^fill" (or "^small fill", "^big fill") in a bar makes the drummer fill at the end of it, and "^stop" makes it a stop-time bar; a line %%style bossa nova under a P: line plays that section in another style from the Style menu, and single parts can follow it, as in %%style Swing; voicing drop2; rhythm charleston; bass two (in a bar, "^style bossa nova" does the same from there to the next section); the Fill on bar and Stop on bar boxes write these for you. The M: line sets the meter: the band plays 3/4 as a jazz waltz and counts 6/8 and 12/8 in dotted quarters.
